questions.q: What's the difference between "it runs" and "it's production ready"?
options: Production readiness means it keeps producing correct answers when nobody's watching, inputs misbehave, and the builder is unavailable — a higher bar than working once while observed
There's no real difference between the two
Production ready just means it runs faster
Production ready only refers to cost, nothing else
questions.explain: A demo pipeline only needs to work once, for one audience, right now; a real pipeline runs unattended for months.

questions.q: Which of the six qualities means someone can tell a pipeline is healthy without opening the code?
options: Observable
Reproducible
Cost-aware
Recoverable
questions.explain: Observability is about visibility into health without needing to inspect the underlying logic directly.

questions.q: What is Lesson 41's taxi dashboard missing that would make it production ready, according to this lesson?
options: A test verifying the KQL query's shape after changes, an alert if the Eventstream stops, a documented cost budget, and a defined rollback process
Nothing — it was already fully production ready as built
It needs an entirely different KQL query, unrelated to production readiness
It needs to be rebuilt using Databricks instead of Fabric
questions.explain: This isn't a criticism of Lesson 41 — it was correctly scoped to teach the pipeline's logic, not its operational surroundings.

questions.q: Why didn't the six production-readiness qualities show up as real constraints in Chapters 1-2?
options: A lesson's demo pipeline only ever needs to work once, for one audience, right now — unlike a real pipeline running for months
Chapters 1-2 already fully addressed all six qualities
KQL and Eventstreams don't support any of these qualities technically
These qualities only apply to Databricks, not Fabric
questions.explain: The gap between a working demo and a production system is exactly what motivates this entire chapter.

questions.q: What does this chapter cover, broadly, across its remaining lessons?
options: CI/CD, environments, testing, observability, cost management, incident response, governance/security, and deployment practice
Only more KQL query syntax
Only Power BI report design
Only how to build additional Eventstreams
questions.explain: This spans Lessons 44 through 69, closing with Lesson 70's finale for the entire course.
